name: Tessellated Optical Denial Drone TODD-2 'Blindspot'
description:
The TODD-2 operates as a swarm-capable photonic denial platform — each individual unit is a flat hexagonal tile roughly 12 cm across, housing a phased array of micro-lensed emitters that produce precisely sculpted coherent light interference patterns. When a single unit detects a target via thermal or motion signature, it positions itself in the subject's visual cone and activates its pattern array, producing a persistent false-geometry overlay in the target's visual field — not blindness, but a convincing spatial hallucination that makes distances, edges, and surfaces unreliable. Targets frequently walk into walls, misjudge step heights, or freeze entirely trying to parse contradictory spatial data.

The TODD-2's genuine tactical edge emerges when multiple units coordinate. Three or more tiles triangulating a single target can produce a full 270-degree interference envelope, effectively trapping the target in a bubble of fabricated geometry. Operators describe the effect as 'putting someone inside a painting.' The swarm communicates via low-power mesh radio with negligible emissions signature, making electronic detection difficult. VANTABLACK MEDIA's involvement in its development is rarely advertised but evident in the emitter array's lineage — it borrows heavily from their immersive architectural projection systems.

The tiles are fragile by drone standards and were never designed for contested airspace. They perform poorly in rain and fail entirely in direct high-lumen environments. Their power cells last approximately 40 minutes at full interference output, after which they return to a designated recovery point or drop to the ground inert.
specifications:
dimensions: 12 cm hexagonal tile, 1.8 cm depth
weight: 0.19 kg per unit
typical deployment: 6–12 units per operation
interference range: Effective up to 4 m per unit
swarm envelope: Up to 270° visual disruption with 3+ coordinated units
effect duration: Persistent while target remains in range
battery life: 38–42 minutes at full output
flight mode: Near-silent ducted-fan hover, ceiling 12 m
failure conditions: Rain, >8,000 lux ambient light, strong RF jamming
countermeasures: Ocular implants with interference filtering (licensed tier), physical blindfold
tactical_use: TODD-2 swarms are used almost exclusively for non-lethal containment, high-value capture operations, and crowd control in enclosed spaces. Security firms use them to immobilize individuals without physical confrontation. Criminal organizations deploy them to disorient guards during heists. The tiles are typically seeded through ventilation access or dropped from a building edge before an operation begins. Experienced operators pre-position recovery nets so tiles can be retrieved — they're expensive and traceable if left behind.
cultural_context: VANTABLACK MEDIA publicly produces immersive installation art and corporate event environments. The TODD-2's existence is one of GLMZ's more poorly-kept open secrets — media critics have noted that the company's flagship 'Sensory Architecture' exhibitions produce strikingly similar disorientation effects to documented TODD-2 deployments. The drone has become associated with a particular kind of violence that the city's upper tier prefers: clean, deniable, and aesthetically coherent. Victims of TODD-2 encounters frequently report lasting difficulty with spatial perception, an effect VANTABLACK's legal team characterizes as 'pre-existing anxiety.'
known_users: Art-world fixers and black market couriers
story_hooks: A prominent architect claims she experienced a TODD-2 attack inside a VANTABLACK MEDIA exhibition opening — but the company's lawyers argue she simply had a dissociative episode during an immersive installation. The line between art and weapon is precisely what's on trial.

Someone is deploying TODD-2 units in the Underbelly transit corridors with no apparent objective — targets are disoriented for forty minutes and then released. No theft, no assault. The pattern suggests rehearsal.

A recovered TODD-2 tile has firmware that doesn't match any known variant. The interference pattern it produces isn't designed to disorient — it's designed to implant a specific false memory of a location the target has never been.

physical_description.visual_profile: A flat, perfectly regular hexagonal tile with a matte charcoal finish. The top surface is dominated by a dense honeycomb array of micro-lenses arranged in concentric patterns around a central hub. The device reads as almost organic—reminiscent of an insect's eye or a cross-section of crystalline mineral. Despite its delicate appearance, it carries an unsettling precision.
physical_description.dimensions: 120 mm across hexagonal face, 18 mm depth. Roughly the size of a coaster, weighs less than two hundred grams.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light. Feels substantial enough to hold confidence, but so light it seems to hover in the palm. Unbalanced weight distribution suggests dense internal architecture packed into minimal volume.
physical_description.primary_material: Advanced polymer composite (likely carbon-reinforced) with integrated optical glass micro-lensing. The hexagonal frame is reinforced at edges with what appears to be aluminum honeycomb.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte charcoal with a subtle iridescent bloom across the lens array—a rainbow oil-slick quality that shifts when viewed at angles. The finish is deliberately light-absorbing; VANTABLACK lineage evident in the near-absence of surface reflection.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal-black primary with iridescent optical purple, cyan, and amber highlights visible across the lensed surface only when light strikes directly. Minimal branding.
physical_description.grip_texture: Beveled hexagonal edges with microscopic grip texture—cool to touch, slightly tacky micro-polymer coating designed to prevent slipping during deployment. Edges are prone to catching on fabric.
distinctive_features: Concentric honeycomb micro-lens array covering 70% of top surface—each lens roughly 2mm diameter, creating hypnotic tessellated pattern
Central hub containing barely-visible thermal and motion sensor apertures
Thin discrete LED indicator ring (red/yellow/green) recessed into the edge—only visible at certain angles
Nearly invisible ducted-fan exhaust ports along the beveled edge—air movement almost inaudible
Hexagonal base showing faint wear marks from deployment and recovery
Etched serial number on underside, extremely small, requiring magnification to read
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: The Drift Monitoring Division stamp (Φ motif integrated into hexagon geometry) laser-etched subtly into one edge, roughly 8mm. VANTABLACK reference buried in micro-text on the underside alongside certification marks and a barcode.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show faint scuff marks on the polymer frame and micro-scratches across lens surfaces from deployment. Some lenses may show minor dust or particulate embedding. Battery charge state is often unknown after operation. Many recovered units bear adhesive residue from deployment netting.
